paragraphs: R' Yishmael, son of R' Elazar Ha Kappar.

Avot de Rabbi Natan 29:5 mentions the four divisions of atonement: Rabbi Matya ben Charash went to visit R' Yishmael, son of R' Elazar Ha Kappar, in Laodicea. But Hyman calls this a scribal error and says it SHOULD READ as the account in Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:6; he refers to his fuller discussion under R' Matya ben Charash.

notes.text: Hyman does not specify the exact name or detail to be replaced with the Jerusalem Talmud reading. The supplied Elazar HaKappar patronym is retained pending that source comparison.

Three saved whole scalars were read: Vilna Avot De Rabbi Natan 29:5 has Yishmael ben Elazar Ha Kappar; Schechter Recension A has Elazar Ha Kappar without Yishmael; Venice Shevuot 1:6 has Matya asking Elazar ben Azaryah about Yishmael's four divisions. These are distinct readings, not a merged family. They clarify the comparison but do not prove exactly which detail Hyman meant to replace or its printed history. Hyman's SHOULD READ force is restored rather than weakened to merely proposes. The trailing he of פ״כט־ה is retained as 29:5 supported by the actual returned reference; Elazar's expansion of ר״א is also supported locally by the supplied heading. Heading titles stay R'; full Rabbi for the visiting Matya is supported by Schechter's exact occurrence, without transferring that title to every uninspected pointer.

Vilna Avot DeRabbi Natan 29:5 names Yishmael son of Elazar HaKappar, while Schechter’s Recension A names Elazar HaKappar. In Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:6, Matya asks Elazar ben Azaryah about Yishmael’s teaching. Yoma 86a places the question in Rome. The consulted Hebrew Mekhilta has Elazar at Laodicea, while its English names Elazar ben HaKappar. In his separate article on Matya, Hyman expressly prefers Shevuot and argues that the academy and Rome settings were later additions in the versions he discusses.
